title: Ephemeral admin sessions, KMS key lifecycle, and audit sign-off
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Objective: Define requirements, acceptance criteria, and sign-off checklist for supporting ephemeral administrator sessions in Private deployments, integrating short-lived KMS/HSM-wrapped keys for operator actions, and ensuring immutable audit trails fit for customer audits.

Scope: This ticket covers the PRD-level requirements and acceptance criteria for: (1) issuing time-bound admin sessions via SSO (SAML/OIDC) with explicit RBAC bindings; (2) a KMS key lifecycle that supports ephemeral data-encryption keys (DEKs) wrapped by a long-term KMS CMK/HSM; (3) audit log immutability, retention, and tamper-evidence; and (4) an operator sign-off checklist for customer onboards and compliance attestations.

Out of scope: UI redesign for the Console, changes to Hosted API pricing, and third-party identity provider certification. Those are tracked in follow-up tickets.

Rationale: Customers in regulated industries asked for tighter operator controls: time-limited privileged sessions, per-session key material, and stronger audit evidence to reduce blast radius and improve forensic capability. Ephemeral session support complements existing RBAC and SSO investments and reduces standing privileged credentials among operator teams.
acceptance_criteria: SSO-Session: Admin sessions can be issued via SAML/OIDC with an explicit 'ephemeral_admin' claim and configurable TTL (default 1h, min 5m, max 24h). Session creation and expiry events are recorded in audit logs.

RBAC: A time-bound role binding (roleBinding.expiry) is enforced such that after session expiry the role no longer grants elevated privileges; enforcement verified via automated test harness that attempts privileged action post-expiry and expects denial.

KMS DEK lifecycle: For actions requiring data decryption or signing, a per-session DEK is generated, wrapped with a customer CMK (HSM-backed where available), and rotated/destroyed at session termination. DEK creation/destruction events must be logged.

HSM fallback: If HSM-backed CMK is unavailable, the system fails open only to a pre-approved fallback CMK with explicit emergency justification recorded; fallback path requires additional alerting to the customer's security contacts.

Audit immutability: Audit logs for session lifecycle, DEK wrapping/unwrapping, and privileged API calls are written to an append-only store (WORM) with cryptographic integrity checks and immutable retention policy configurable per-customer (30/90/365 days).

Evidence collection: The operational export contains session token hash, SSO assertion id, RBAC binding id, DEK wrap ciphertext, and API trace ids for all privileged operations for at least the configured retention period.

Tests & Automation: Unit and e2e tests simulate session issuance, privilege escalation, key wrap/unwrapping, and verify audit records inserted and immutability proof checks pass. Tests must be green in CI for release.
signoff_checklist: PM review: PRD reviewed and approved by Product (Aisha Patel) and Security PM (Ivan Morales).
Security review: Security engineering must provide threat model and approve cryptographic choices (HSM/CMK parameters).
Legal & Compliance: Compliance team confirms retention policy options meet SOC2 and EU customer requirements for selected customers.
Infra readiness: Dedicated infra capacity and KMS quotas validated for private deployments (ENG sign-off).
E2E validation: QA evidence attached showing CI tests and an integration run against a staging private-deploy cluster.
Runbook & Ops: Operator runbook for emergency key fallback and forensic export documented and reviewed by SRE.
Customer onboarding checklist: Template email and evidence package verified for first customer pilot.
Signatures: Final sign-off captured from (Product Lead, Security Eng Lead, SRE Lead, Legal).
decisions: 2025-01-30 Decision: Default ephemeral session TTL set to 1 hour; configurable per-customer with enforced maximum of 24 hours to limit dwell time.
2025-01-31 Decision: Use envelope encryption model: per-session DEK generated on compute host, wrapped by customer's CMK in KMS. This avoids holding plaintext DEKs in long term storage.

2025-02-02 Decision: Audit logs will be written to internal blobstore with SHA-256 chained digests to provide tamper evidence; long-term retention options will include pushing to customer-controlled S3 for extra assurance.

risk_assessment: Medium: introduces complexity in key lifecycle and runtime state; potential latency increase on first privileged operation due to DEK generation and wrap. Mitigations include async pre-warm and limited-scope rate limiting for initial session setup.
qa_plan: Unit tests for token TTL enforcement and RBAC expiry behavior.
Integration tests that create ephemeral session, perform privileged action, and verify post-expiry access denied.
Crypto tests that simulate KMS failure and validate fallback CMK path and alerting behavior.
Audit tamper checks that validate SHA-256 chaining across a synthetic workload and verify immutability proofs in CI.
rollback_plan: If significant regressions are observed in staging (high error rate or key management failures), revert runtime changes and disable ephemeral session issuance via feature flag. Notify affected pilot customers and schedule hotfix.
